📖 Quick Definitions: Ratify = make legally binding law • Proliferation = spread of nukes to new states • Tactical vs. Strategic = battlefield vs. long-range city nukes • Denial = stopping an invasion conventionally
1. Ratify (vs. Sign): Formally approve a treaty by parliament so it becomes binding law (signing alone is non-binding).
2. European NATO (30 States): All 32 NATO allies except the US & Canada; includes nuclear-armed UK & France + 5 B61 host states.
3. TPNW: 2017 UN treaty (in force 2021) banning developing, possessing, hosting, or assisting nuclear weapons.
4. Nuclear Sharing (B61-12): Storing ~100 US-owned gravity bombs at 6 bases in Germany, Belgium, Italy, Netherlands & Türkiye.
5. Tactical vs. Strategic: Tactical = shorter-range battlefield warheads; Strategic = long-range ICBMs/submarines.
6. Deterrence by Denial: Stopping an invasion on the battlefield with conventional stealth jets & precision missiles.
7. Extended Deterrence (Umbrella): A nuclear nation's promise to protect non-nuclear allies with its nuclear arsenal.
8. Permissive Action Links (PALs): Coded electronic locks on US warheads requiring the US President's launch codes.
9. Proliferation: The spread of nuclear weapons to countries that don't currently have them (e.g., Poland).
10. Euratom & IAEA Protocol: Binding European Union & UN nuclear inspections that verify zero hidden warheads.
11. Divestment / Preemptive: Divestment = pulling bank money out of nuke makers; Preemptive = striking first to destroy bases.
12. Escalation Dominance: Controlling the upper hand at the next level of war so the other side is forced to back down.

Four tests every card has to pass. If one of theirs fails, say the line out loud and ask the judge to drop it. Check your own cards against the same four.

Varsity rule: a good debater reads a quote; a varsity debater explains why the person who said it is the most qualified person in the room. Every card in 🗂 Source Cards now opens with the author's credentials.
